why: classification_metrics.v1 computes metric_identity_sha256 from author_primary_metric, so the digest is a TERMINAL-LEVEL tag that binds the receipt's PRIMARY metric only.
A receipt's secondary, naive, probability, coverage and confusion rows therefore inherit an identity that is not their own.

Proved against the live warehouse on 2026-09-29: macro-F1 0.9467546527629132 stands under identity 1756f877 (an ACCURACY identity) on unit native-accuracy and under a62f184c (a MACRO_F1 identity) on unit native-macro-f1, while identity 1756f877 also covers macro-F1 0.9252733932274245 on unit framework-accuracy.

So classification_metrics.v1's guidance that two rows agree only when their identity digests agree is UNSOUND FOR SECONDARY ROWS, and an aggregate keyed on the terminal-level digest would combine rows that measure different things, or the same thing twice.

This document does not edit classification_metrics.v1 and does not rewrite a stored row. It is a successor contract: every classification_metrics.v1 producer must additionally emit the tags declared here, and a reader recomputes any row's identity from the stored tags alone.

identity_inputs.note: What the number in THIS row MEANS. Nothing about who measured it, on what, or how well.

deliberately_excluded.author_name: the author's own label for a metric is attribution, not meaning; it is carried as reported_under_name and is refused by name in compare(), rather than hidden inside a digest. Keeping it out is what lets a PRIMARY macro-F1 row and a SECONDARY macro-F1 row on the same labels and denominator share one identity, which is the only way a double count between two terminals can be detected at all.
deliberately_excluded.row_role: a value does not change meaning because the receipt that carried it called it primary; if row_role entered the identity, the same measurement stored twice under two roles would hide behind two digests.
deliberately_excluded.evidence_class: SEPARATE DIMENSION. A PUBLISHED_REFERENCE accuracy and a MEASUREMENT accuracy of the same definition are comparable, which is exactly why they must not be averaged: comparability belongs in the identity, provenance belongs beside it.
deliberately_excluded.value: an identity that changed with the value would make every row unique and could never detect a duplicate.
deliberately_excluded.provider_checkpoint_population_protocol: those decide WHICH measurement this is, not what it means; they belong to the occurrence key.

occurrence_inputs.note: What was measured, once. Two rows with one occurrence key are ONE measurement and count ONCE.

deliberately_excluded.row_role: so the SAME measurement carried as a primary in one terminal and as a secondary in another collapses to one occurrence instead of being counted twice.
deliberately_excluded.terminal_sha256_campaign_unit_generation: a double count BETWEEN terminals is the failure this key exists to catch; a key that carried the terminal could not catch it.
deliberately_excluded.receipt_sha256: two receipts of one measurement are two reports, not two measurements.

occurrence_inputs.replicates: protocol_sha256, scorer_sha256 and seed are IN the key, so a genuine re-measurement under a different protocol, scorer or seed is a distinct occurrence and is never silently deduplicated away.

aggregation_rule: GROUP BY metric_row_identity_sha256 AND evidence_class. Never by metric alone, never by value, never by the terminal-level metric_identity_sha256.
Within a group, DEDUPLICATE ON metric_occurrence_sha256 before any mean, count or ranking.
Two rows that share an occurrence key and disagree in value are a refusal (CONFLICTING_VALUES_FOR_ONE_OCCURRENCE), never an average.
A group that mixes evidence classes is a refusal (EVIDENCE_CLASSES_MIXED_IN_ONE_AGGREGATE); split it, do not weight it.
over_budget_note: A 77-class confusion contributes 308 rows, whose per-row digests do not fit in a tag. The map digests always cover EVERY row; the JSON maps carry the rows that fit and otherwise the sentinel, and any row's digest is recomputable from the stored tags with recompute_from_tags(tags, metric_key).

kinds.PROBABILITY_METRIC: a scalar over predicted probabilities on the evaluation population
kinds.POPULATION_SHARE: a fraction of the evaluation population, not a score
kinds.CONFUSION_COUNT: a count of rows in one cell of the reference x predicted matrix

denominator_policy_rule: Every family-bearing row takes the governing denominator policy, which is abstention.denominator_policy, and a receipt whose author_primary_metric.denominator_policy differs from it is refused by name (PRIMARY_AND_ABSTENTION_DENOMINATOR_POLICIES_DISAGREE): classification_metrics.v1 already checks every carried value against the confusion under the abstention policy, so a second, different policy on the primary would make the receipt's own consistency check measure something the digest does not.

refusals.ROW_IDENTITY_TAGS_MISSING: a classification_metrics.v1 terminal without these tags; its secondary rows would inherit the primary's identity
refusals.DOUBLE_COUNT_SAME_OCCURRENCE_ACROSS_TERM: two stored rows are one measurement; counted once, and reported as dropped
refusals.EVIDENCE_CLASSES_MIXED_IN_ONE_AGGREGATE: a measured and a published value in one mean
